title: The Afternoon Brief: SEC vote looms today as US Open, NFL openers add layers
dek: The SEC's expulsion vote on LSU is scheduled for today, the same day the desk's morning report on the standoff still awaits resolution, while overnight tennis and NFL results add new threads to a busy sports Thursday.
author: GoCheckMySports
bottom_line: Today's scheduled SEC vote on expelling LSU, the first such vote in the conference's 94-year history, anchors a day when several sports institutions are testing the limits of their own authority, from the CFP's negotiating window with ESPN over playoff expansion to the Big Ten's new replay-transparency rules. The honest read is that none of these processes concluded today: the SEC vote outcome, the CFP-ESPN talks running to December 1, and the Louisiana court injunction's interaction with conference discipline all remain open. Overnight, American men guaranteed their first US Open finalist since 2003 with Shelton and Tiafoe both reaching the semifinal, and the Seahawks opened the NFL season with a 13-10 win over the Patriots complicated by Sam Darnold's hip injury. Watch for today's SEC vote count, further testing on Darnold, Friday's Shelton-Tiafoe semifinal, and the Big Ten's replay-audio debut on September 12.
body: The day's central fact remains the same one flagged this morning: the SEC is scheduled to vote today on whether to expel LSU, the first such vote in the conference's 94-year history. That has not changed since the morning brief. What has moved is the surrounding context, an amended federal complaint filed Tuesday that adds LSU Board of Supervisors members and Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill as defendants, and seeks a declaratory judgment that LSU's conduct violated the SEC's rules. The conference's proposed penalties include a 50 percent fine of the sport's operating budget, a 50 percent suspension of head coach Lane Kiffin for the season, and revocation of SEC voting privileges. LSU voted in favor of a professional player ban but abstained on penalties, and a Louisiana state court has already issued a preliminary injunction clearing the two players in question, tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, to compete, a fact that sets state and conference authority on a collision course regardless of today's vote.

Alongside the LSU matter, college football's governance is moving on a second front: the College Football Playoff triggered a 30-day negotiating window with ESPN on September 8 over a possible 24-team playoff beginning in 2027, a shift that would eliminate conference championship games and require ESPN to account for at least $200 million in lost annual media value from those games, per ESPN's reporting. The CFP's own statement is careful to say this is not a decision to expand, only an opening to gather information, with a December 1 deadline for a final call. That same date is when conferences must tell broadcast partners whether they will drop championship games, tying the playoff format question to media contracts across the sport.

Overnight, the US Open produced two threads. Ben Shelton beat top-ranked defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) in a match that ended at 3:33 a.m. ET on September 9, the latest finish in tournament history, ending Alcaraz's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak. Frances Tiafoe came back from two sets and a break down to beat Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6), the first such comeback in a US Open men's quarterfinal since 2014. The two Americans meet in Friday's semifinal, guaranteeing the tournament's first Black American men's finalist since Arthur Ashe in 1972 and the country's first shot at a men's major title since 2003.

In the NFL, the Seahawks beat the Patriots 13-10 in the season opener, a rematch of last year's Super Bowl decided by Patriots QB Drake Maye's interception to Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe with 26 seconds left, on third-and-5 from the Seattle 16 with field-goal range in reach. NBC's Cris Collinsworth called the throw indefensible given the situation. Seattle's own quarterback situation is unsettled too: Sam Darnold left with a hip injury on the opening drive and did not return, though a fracture was ruled out; Drew Lock finished the game, and further testing on Darnold was pending as of Wednesday night. Separately, the Big Ten announced it will broadcast live replay-review audio for all conference games and Big Ten-officiated home non-conference games starting Saturday, September 12, a response to the disputed extra second that decided last weekend's Michigan-Western Michigan finish.

Elsewhere, the College Sports Commission cleared more than $227 million in NIL deals in July and August, nearly double the total value cleared in its first full year of operation, with 7,639 deals processed and 68 percent resolved within seven days. The Rugby Football Union will extend Steve Borthwick's contract past the 2028 Six Nations to provide stability heading into the 2027 World Cup in Australia, though his tenure beyond the tournament depends on results there, according to performance director Conor O'Shea. The Dodgers called up outfielder Josue De Paula, MLB Pipeline's No. 6 overall prospect, to debut Friday in Miami after placing Shohei Ohtani on the 15-day injured list with left knee and right biceps injuries.

The throughline across today's biggest stories is institutions testing how much authority they actually hold. The SEC is testing whether a two-thirds vote can expel a member for the first time in 94 years while a state court injunction already complicates enforcement. The CFP is testing whether ESPN will accept a format shift that erases hundreds of millions in existing championship-game value. The Big Ten is testing whether transparency in replay audio actually resolves disputes rather than just broadcasting them. None of these questions resolve today; today only marks when each test begins in earnest.
No desk boards were available this run, so the read above rests entirely on the day's published reporting rather than live league data.

What to watch: the outcome of today's SEC vote on LSU expulsion and whether the two-thirds threshold is met; whether the Louisiana state court injunction and any federal ruling create conflicting mandates; the CFP-ESPN negotiating window running through the December 1 deadline; Friday's Shelton-Tiafoe US Open semifinal and the September 12 women's semifinals; the Big Ten's new replay-audio rollout beginning Saturday; and further word on Sam Darnold's hip injury ahead of Seattle's Week 2 game.
